- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment turns bearish sharply (drop >0.50) and prices are trending down, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to match sentiment shift.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” rule: subtract 1–2% from forecast for 2–3 periods post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67) and prices show mean reversion, model often holds too high; use 1–2% downward bias for 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is low, model tends to ignore sentiment; apply a “sentiment lag” correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 1–2 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in high-news environments; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if news volume >2.0 and sentiment >0.50.
